title: How to Do Lunges Properly for Beginners (Leg Workout at Home)
intro: The lunge is a one-leg-at-a-time exercise that trains your thighs, glutes and balance. It only needs space for two steps and can be done at home or at the office.
muscles: Front thighs (quadriceps), glutes, back thighs (hamstrings), calves and core for balance. Lunges strengthen and shape your leg muscles, but they don't burn thigh fat specifically. Thigh fat goes down when your whole body loses fat.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, hands on your hips.
Step forward with one leg, a moderately long step.
Lower your body until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Make sure your front knee is in line with your toes, body upright.
Push through the heel of your front foot to stand back up.
mistakes: Front knee caving inward. Push your knee slightly outward so it's in line with your second and third toes.
Step too short until your front heel lifts. Step further so your foot stays flat.
Leaning forward. Keep your chest up and look ahead.
easier: Do a static split squat: stay in the step position and just go up and down, while holding a chair or wall. Reverse lunges (stepping back) are also usually kinder to the knees.
harder: Do walking lunges along a corridor, or hold for 2 seconds at the bottom of each rep. Once you're strong, try jump lunges slowly and with control.
dose: Beginner: 2-3 sets x 8-10 reps per leg, rest 60 seconds. Do it 2-3 times a week, not on back-to-back days.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your knee or hip. If you have knee problems, a past ligament injury or feel unstable, see a doctor or physiotherapist before continuing.

faq.q: Can lunges make my thighs smaller?
faq.a: Lunges strengthen your thigh and glute muscles, so your legs look firmer. But thigh fat can't be burned from there alone. It goes down when your body as a whole loses fat through eating and daily movement.

faq.q: My knees click during lunges. Is that dangerous?
faq.a: Clicking without pain is usually normal. But if it clicks with pain or swelling, stop and get it checked. Try reverse lunges and shorten the range first.

faq.q: Which is better, forward or backward lunges?
faq.a: For beginners, backward lunges (reverse lunges) are easier to control and put less stress on the knees. Once you're confident, you can mix both.
